items.raw_snippet: # Cycclone, Inc. Announces Agreement in Principle for the Acquisition of AI Robotics Company. (OTCID:CYCL) today acknowledges reaching an agreement in principle to acquire an AI Robotics design, develop and manufacturing company under the newly formed division, Cycclone Ai Robotics. Recently an agreement in principle has been reached for Cycclone to acquire an American AI Robotics company based in California. At present, the base manufacturing is carried out in Europe, and Cycclone management has started the work to bring a manufacturing facility to Australia and another facility in the United States of America. "If successful, we will be able to bring a base industrial manufacturing platform to assimilate further work on our engines and as a bonus, the company has a "Space Division" to supply products for the new space program and as some people know, I am a bit of a space nut". items.snippet: # AI Is Changing How Consultants Get Paid—and Much More, BCG’s CEO Says. Christo...
items.raw_snippet: # AI Is Changing How Consultants Get Paid—and Much More, BCG’s CEO Says. Christoph Schweizer points to higher revenues and head count in response to predictions the technology is killing his industry. *This article is republished with permission from The Wall Street Journal. For all the doomsday predictions that AI will make management consultants obsolete, Boston Consulting Group CEO Christoph Schweizer has this retort: Look at the business. Revenue at BCG rose 7% to $14.4 billion in the firm’s latest fiscal year and its head count is expanding as the firm rushes to meet a near “infinite need” from companies for help rolling out AI, Schweizer said. The Wall Street Journal talked with Schweizer about AI and pricing, entry-level hiring and whether Anthropic poses a competitive threat. At this point, there’s a lot of commentary that the industry is moving more towards value-based fee arrangements. **WSJ:** What does your hiring look like at the entry level—are you changing how many people you bring into the firm given that AI can do things differently?

items.snippet: They are operational, contractual, regulatory, and increasingly tied to day-to-d...
items.raw_snippet: They are operational, contractual, regulatory, and increasingly tied to day-to-day business risk. KJK helps businesses evaluate, implement, govern, and defend their use of AI technologies through practical legal and operational guidance aligned with how organizations actually function. We advise clients across the full lifecycle of AI adoption, from internal use policies and vendor agreements to disclosure architecture, litigation readiness, regulatory response, and AI-related disputes. Businesses across industries are integrating AI into internal workflows, customer-facing operations, data analysis, hiring processes, content generation, software development, and decision-making systems. The challenge is applying those frameworks in a way that reflects how businesses actually operate and how AI tools are being used in practice. KJK’s AI Strategy, Risk Management & Compliance practice works with companies across the full lifecycle of AI adoption, from evaluation and implementation to governance, commercialization, disputes, and ongoing operational oversight. We help clients translate evolving legal expectations into practical operational frameworks aligned with how their organizations function day to day.
